To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nuclear modification factor RAA is a strong function of the collision centrality, the particle mass and the particle type (baryon versus meson), that the baryon to pion ratio at mid-rapidity is a strong function only of the particle type (meson versus baryon), that the scaling properties of the elliptic flow coefficient v2 are consistent with a hydrodynamic picture, and that the elliptic flow is not suppressed in d+Au relative to p+p collisions

the suppression of the yield of hadrons at intermediate transverse momentum in Au+Au at RHIC is consistent with the suppression expected from parton energy loss, that the suppression in d+Au at RHICH is consistent with that from parton energy in cold nuclear matter, that the suppression of hadrons at high transverse momentum in p+p is consistent with the expectation from perturbative QCD, that the suppression is consistent with a common mechanism for parton energy loss in Au+Au and

The nuclear modification factor, RA, for charged particles is found to be approximately constant as a function of transverse momentum, pt, for 1 < pt < 4 GeV/c for central collisions in both Au+Au and Cu+Cu at sqrt(s_NN) = 62.4 and 200 GeV, and in p+p and d+Au at 200 GeV.

the partonic nature of the matter produced in the collisions at RHIC is clearly demonstrated.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the quark and gluon degrees of freedom are the dominant constituents of the hot dense matter produced in heavy ion collisions.
the initial geometry of the collisions plays an important role in determining the final state observables.
the initial state of heavy ion collisions is not simply a dilution of the parton distributions of nucleons.
